description: Your 74-year-old mother is visiting for a month and will use your Mac daily. She has age-related macular degeneration (makes low-contrast text hard to read and bright screens painful) and moderate arthritis in her hands (makes simultaneous key combinations difficult). Before she arrives, open System Settings and configure the Accessibility settings so the Mac is comfortable for her. You need to: (1) enable Increase Contrast under Display settings in Accessibility, (2) enable Reduce Transparency under Display settings in Accessibility, (3) increase the pointer cursor size to at least 3× the default (the slider has a range — move it well to the right), (4) enable the scroll gesture with a modifier key to zoom in (under Zoom in Accessibility), (5) enable Sticky Keys under Motor control in Keyboard settings in Accessibility, and (6) enable Slow Keys under Motor control in Keyboard settings in Accessibility. All six changes must persist after you finish — the verifier reads the com.apple.universalaccess defaults domain.

metadata.scenario: family/personal-use — configuring Mac for elderly parent with vision and motor difficulties
